This suggests that from 448 K (low) to 523 K (moderately high temperature) and less than 40 to 70 MPa of applied stress, excluding 523 K/60 to 70 MPa, diffusion creep is the rate-controlling mechanism for Alloy-1.
From the values of stress exponent and activation energy, it is evident that the governing creep mechanism for Alloy-2 is similar to Alloy-1; namely diffusion creep is the rate-controlling mechanism.
The increased diffusion rate along grain boundaries leads to grain boundary sliding at 523 K/40 to 70 MPa.
At low to moderately high temperatures (0.48 to 0.53 Tm of pure Al) and at 40 to 70 MPa of applied stress, diffusion creep is the rate-controlling mech-anism in both Alloy-1 and Alloy-2.
